request: how many litres does a 50 by 30 by 40 cm fish tank hold?

beats.intent: A fish tank 50 cm long, 30 cm deep and 40 cm tall
beats.narration: A fish tank is fifty centimetres long, thirty deep and forty tall.
beats.code:
stage.title("Litres in a fish tank")
k = 0.07
o = np.array([-5.8, -2.0, 0])
W, H = 50 * k * RIGHT, 40 * k * UP
D = 30 * k * 0.5 * np.array([1, 1, 0])
front = Polygon(o, o + W, o + W + H, o + H, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.25)
top = Polygon(o + H, o + W + H, o + W + H + D, o + H + D, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.15)
side = Polygon(o + W, o + W + D, o + W + D + H, o + W + H, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.1)
stage.play(Create(front), Create(top), Create(side))
stage.add(front, top, side)
stage.label(Line(o, o + W), "50 cm", direction=DOWN)
stage.label(Line(o, o + H), "40 cm", direction=LEFT)
stage.label(Line(o + W, o + W + D), "30 cm", direction=DR)

beats.intent: The tank filled with water, its volume 50 × 30 × 40 cm³
beats.narration: Fill it. Its volume is length times depth times height.
beats.code:
stage.play(front.animate.set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.6), top.animate.set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.4), side.animate.set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.35))
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("60 000 cm³", font_size=30).move_to(front)))

beats.intent: A single 10 cm cube beside the tank, labelled 1 litre = 1000 cm³
beats.narration: A litre is a cube ten centimetres on each side: a thousand cubic centimetres.
beats.code:
cube = Square(10 * k * 1.6, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.6).move_to([0.4, -1.2, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(cube))
stage.add(cube)
stage.label(cube, "1 L = 1000 cm³", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The tank beside 50 × 30 × 40 = 60 000 cm³ and 60 000 ÷ 1000 = 60 L
beats.narration: Sixty thousand cubic centimetres divided by a thousand is sixty litres.

request: how many posts do you need for a 20 m fence with a post every 2 m?

beats.intent: A 20 m line for the fence
beats.narration: A fence runs twenty metres, with a post every two metres. Twenty divided by two is ten, but is that the number of posts?
beats.code:
stage.title("Fence posts")
k = 0.5
x0 = -5.2
line = Line([x0, -0.6, 0], [x0 + 20 * k, -0.6, 0], color=GREY_B)
stage.play(Create(line))
stage.add(line)
stage.label(line, "20 m", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: Ten 2 m gaps marked along the line
beats.narration: There are ten gaps of two metres.
beats.code:
gaps = VGroup(*[Line([x0 + 2 * i * k, -0.6, 0], [x0 + 2 * (i + 1) * k, -0.6, 0], color=BLUE if i % 2 else YELLOW, stroke_width=10) for i in range(10)])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(g) for g in gaps], lag_ratio=0.1))
stage.add(gaps)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("10 gaps", font_size=28, color=BLUE).move_to([x0 + 10 * k, 0.3, 0])))

beats.intent: Posts at every boundary, including both ends: 11 posts
beats.narration: But a post sits at both ends of every gap, including the very first and the very last. That's eleven posts.
beats.code:
posts = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=0.12, height=0.9, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to([x0 + 2 * i * k, -0.25, 0]) for i in range(11)])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowFromEdge(p, DOWN) for p in posts], lag_ratio=0.1))
stage.add(posts)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("11 posts", font_size=28, color=ORANGE).move_to([x0 + 10 * k, 1.0, 0])))

beats.narration: Posts are always one more than gaps on a straight fence.

request: why does light bounce off a mirror at the same angle it hits it?

beats.intent: A flat mirror with a dashed normal line standing up from it
beats.narration: Light hits a flat mirror. Draw the normal: a line at right angles to the mirror where the light lands.
beats.code:
stage.title("Reflection")
P = np.array([-3, -1.8, 0])
mirror = Line(P + 3.2 * LEFT, P + 3.2 * RIGHT, color=GREY_B, stroke_width=8)
normal = DashedLine(P, P + 3.6 * UP, color=WHITE)
stage.play(Create(mirror), Create(normal))
stage.add(mirror, normal)
stage.label(mirror, "mirror", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: An incoming ray at 40° to the normal hitting the mirror
beats.narration: A ray comes in at forty degrees to the normal.
beats.code:
src = P + 3.4 * np.array([-np.sin(40 * DEGREES), np.cos(40 * DEGREES), 0])
inc = Arrow(src, P, buff=0, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=5)
stage.play(GrowArrow(inc))
stage.add(inc)
a_in = Angle(Line(P, P + UP), Line(P, src), radius=0.9, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(a_in))
stage.add(a_in)
stage.label(a_in, "40°", direction=UL, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The reflected ray leaving at 40° on the other side of the normal
beats.narration: It leaves at exactly the same angle on the other side: forty degrees.
beats.code:
out_end = P + 3.4 * np.array([np.sin(40 * DEGREES), np.cos(40 * DEGREES), 0])
ref = Arrow(P, out_end, buff=0, color=ORANGE, stroke_width=5)
stage.play(GrowArrow(ref))
stage.add(ref)
a_out = Angle(Line(P, out_end), Line(P, P + UP), radius=0.9, color=ORANGE)
stage.play(Create(a_out))
stage.add(a_out)
stage.label(a_out, "40°", direction=UR, color=ORANGE)

beats.intent: The picture beside angle of incidence = angle of reflection
beats.narration: The angle in equals the angle out, both measured from the normal. It's like a ball bouncing off a smooth wall.

request: when a cross-shaped net folds into a dice, which faces end up opposite?

beats.intent: A cross-shaped net of six squares numbered 1 to 6
beats.narration: Here's a net of six squares in a cross, numbered one to six. Fold it up and it makes a dice.
beats.code:
stage.title("Folding a dice")
s = 0.9
c = np.array([-3.4, -0.2, 0])
cells = {1: (0, 1), 2: (-1, 0), 3: (0, 0), 4: (1, 0), 5: (0, -1), 6: (0, -2)}
net = VGroup()
for n, (i, j) in cells.items():
    net.add(VGroup(Square(s, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.1), Text(str(n), font_size=32)).move_to(c + s * np.array([i, j, 0])))
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(sq) for sq in net], lag_ratio=0.15))
stage.add(net)

beats.intent: 1 and 5 coloured the same: in the long column they have exactly one square between them
beats.narration: Look down the long column: one, three, five, six. Two squares with exactly one square between them in a straight line fold to opposite sides. So one is opposite five.

beats.intent: 3 and 6 coloured together, then 2 and 4 across the middle row
beats.narration: By the same rule, three is opposite six, and in the middle row two is opposite four.
beats.code:
stage.play(net[2][0].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.6), net[5][0].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.6))
stage.play(net[1][0].animate.set_fill(ORANGE, opacity=0.6), net[3][0].animate.set_fill(ORANGE, opacity=0.6))
stage.label(net, "same colour = opposite faces", direction=RIGHT)

beats.intent: The net beside the opposite pairs 1 + 5 = 6, 2 + 4 = 6, 3 + 6 = 9
beats.narration: The opposite pairs add to six, six and nine. On a real dice opposite faces always add to seven, so this numbering would not make a real dice.
